<!-- Generated by `pnpm exec nx run shared-events:schema-export` from libs/shared/events. Do not edit by hand. -->

An event records something that happened in QAuth: a sign-in, a refused token request, a new
client. Events exist so that automation outside QAuth can act on them
([ADR-018 §3](/reference/records/adr/018-1-0-scope-and-stability/)). ADR-018 names four routes
for them: signed webhooks in the Standard Webhooks format, a cursor-based event API, Shared Signals
Framework streams, and OpenTelemetry export. Every route carries the same event, in the envelope
below. The event types and their payload schemas are part of the 1.0 stability contract (ADR-018
§5).

This page is generated from the type registry in `libs/shared/events`, together with the JSON
Schema files it links.

## The envelope

Every event has these members. `type`, `category` and `data` depend on the type; the
others mean the same for every type. A member that does not apply is absent, never `null`.

```json
{
  "id": "0199f2b4-7c3e-7a51-9d2b-3a6c8e1f0a42",
  "type": "urn:qauth:event:user.signed_in:v1",
  "time": "2026-10-22T09:30:00.123Z",
  "realm": "0199f2b4-1a2b-7c3d-8e4f-5a6b7c8d9e0f",
  "category": "user",
  "actor": {
    "type": "user",
    "id": "0199f2b4-2b3c-7d4e-9f5a-6b7c8d9e0f1a"
  },
  "subject": {
    "type": "user",
    "id": "0199f2b4-2b3c-7d4e-9f5a-6b7c8d9e0f1a"
  },
  "client": {
    "id": "notes-app"
  },
  "request": {
    "traceId": "req-7f3a",
    "ip": "203.0.113.7",
    "userAgent": "Mozilla/5.0"
  },
  "data": {
    "method": "password"
  }
}
```

| Member                  | Type                                                                | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                    | UUID                                                                | yes      | The event id, a UUIDv7. One event keeps one id on every route and every retry, so a receiver drops duplicates by it. It is the `webhook-id` of a webhook and the source of an SSF `jti`.                                                                              |
| `type`                  | string                                                              | yes      | The event type, `urn:qauth:event:<name>:v<N>`. The registry lists every type.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `time`                  | time (RFC 3339, UTC)                                                | yes      | When the event happened, as an RFC 3339 time in UTC. Not when it was delivered.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `realm`                 | UUID                                                                | yes      | The id of the realm the event happened in.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `category`              | one of `user`, `admin`                                              | yes      | `user`: an end user's own activity. `admin`: an administrator's change. Fixed by the type.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `actor`                 | object                                                              | no       | Who or what caused the event.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `actor.type`            | one of `user`, `client`, `system`, `operator_cli`, or a later value | yes      | `user`: a person, signed in. `client`: an OAuth client acting for itself or, with `delegationChain`, as an agent for the subject. `system`: QAuth itself, such as a scheduled job. `operator_cli`: an operator on the server host, through a QAuth command-line tool. |
| `actor.id`              | string                                                              | no       | The actor's identifier: a user id, a client's `client_id`, or the operating-system user for `operator_cli`. Absent for `system`.                                                                                                                                      |
| `actor.delegationChain` | array of string                                                     | no       | The RFC 8693 `act` chain of a delegated request, as `client_id` values: the acting agent first, then each earlier actor. Absent when nothing was delegated.                                                                                                           |
| `subject`               | object                                                              | no       | What the event is about.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `subject.type`          | one of `user`, `client`, `api_key`, or a later value                | yes      | What kind of thing the subject is.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `subject.id`            | string                                                              | yes      | The subject's identifier: a user id, a client's `client_id` or an API key id. It stays valid after the subject is deleted.                                                                                                                                            |
| `client`                | object                                                              | no       | The OAuth client the request came through.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `client.id`             | string                                                              | yes      | The client's `client_id`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `request`               | object                                                              | no       | The HTTP request that caused the event.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `request.traceId`       | string                                                              | no       | The id under which QAuth logged the request: the `trace_id` of a problem document from the same request.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `request.ip`            | IPv4 address or IPv6 address                                        | no       | The end user's IP address, as QAuth derived it from the request.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `request.userAgent`     | string                                                              | no       | The `User-Agent` header, cut to 1024 characters.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `data`                  | object                                                              | yes      | The type's own payload. Its schema is the type's.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

- The `id` is a UUIDv7, assigned once when the event is recorded. A retry, a redelivery and
  every route repeat it, so a receiver drops duplicates by it. A webhook's `webhook-id` header is
  the event id, and an SSF Security Event Token's `jti` is derived from it.
- The `subject` is a plain id with no database link: it stays valid after the user or the client
  is deleted.
- A webhook body is the envelope. Standard Webhooks recommends a full-stop delimited `type`, a
  `timestamp` and `data`: the short name in the middle of the identifier is the delimited type,
  and `time` is the timestamp.
- The envelope's schema is [envelope.json](/schemas/events/envelope.json).

## Payload rules

These rules hold for every event's `data`. They were written for the audit log
([ADR-011 §8](/reference/records/adr/011-enterprise-managed-authorization/),
[ADR-017 §11](/reference/records/adr/017-first-party-login/)) and apply to events.

1. **Ids, not names or addresses.** `data` names a user, a client or a record by its id. A type
   that needs a name, an email address, a phone number or an IP address declares that field in
   its registry entry. No type registered today does.
2. **Never a secret.** No password, code, OTP, token, key, assertion, signature, cookie, secret,
   or set-up or reset link, in any form. There is no exception.
3. **Hidden identifiers are keyed HMACs.** An identifier that must not be revealed, such as the
   address a failed sign-in typed, is carried as an HMAC under a server-side key, never as the
   value and never as a plain hash.

A scanner enforces the rules. The registry's tests fail when a type's schema declares a field
named like a secret, or like personal data the type has not declared. `parseEvent`, the check a
single event passes before it is stored or sent, applies them again: a field named like a secret,
or a value shaped like a token or a key, refuses the event. The scanner reads names, so a field that holds an
id, a type or a count of such a thing passes when its name ends in `Id`, `Type` or `Count`
(`apiKeyId`, `issuedTokenType`).

## Versioning

An event type's identifier is `urn:qauth:event:<name>:v<N>`. The `<name>` is its short
name: lower-case `snake_case` segments joined by full stops, the resource first. `<N>` is the
major version of its `data`. Every QAuth-defined identifier carries a version (ADR-018 §5).

Within a major release, the contract changes only by addition:

- a new type, which is a new entry in the registry;
- a new optional member of a type's `data`, or of the envelope;
- a new value of an open set (`x-extensible-enum`, shown on this page as "or a later value").

Anything else is a breaking change: removing or renaming a member, changing its type, making a
member required, adding a required member, or narrowing what a member accepts. A breaking change
makes a new type with the next version, such as `:v2`. QAuth emits both versions for every
event until the deprecation window ends, so a receiver moves at its own pace. The old type is
marked deprecated and names its replacement. It is removed only in a new major release, no sooner
than 12 months after the deprecation (ADR-018 §5).

A receiver ignores members it does not know, and accepts a value of an open set it does not know.
The published schemas leave objects open for that reason. A closed set, such as `category`, does
not grow within a major release.

The stable-surface check compares each schema file with the last release and fails on a breaking
change that no one approved.

## Schemas

Each type has a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of its whole event: the envelope, with `type`,
`category` and `data` fixed to the type. They are served under `/schemas/events/`, and each
file's `$id` is its URL. The envelope's own schema accepts an event of any type.

### user.signed_in v1

A person signed in: the credential checked out and QAuth started a browser session or issued tokens.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:user.signed_in:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`
- Schema: [user.signed_in.v1.json](/schemas/events/user.signed_in.v1.json)

| Member            | Type                                          | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `method`          | one of `password`, `wallet`, or a later value | yes      | `password`: an identifier and a password. `wallet`: a credential presented from a wallet (OpenID4VP). The set may grow in a minor release. |
| `verifierProfile` | string                                        | no       | The verifier profile the wallet presentation was checked under, such as `haip-1.0`.                                                        |

### user.sign_in_failed v1

A sign-in was refused: an unknown identifier, a wrong credential, a locked or disabled account.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:user.sign_in_failed:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `warning` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`
- Schema: [user.sign_in_failed.v1.json](/schemas/events/user.sign_in_failed.v1.json)

| Member            | Type                                          | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `method`          | one of `password`, `wallet`, or a later value | yes      | `password`: an identifier and a password. `wallet`: a credential presented from a wallet (OpenID4VP). The set may grow in a minor release.                                                                                     |
| `reason`          | string                                        | yes      | Why, as a `snake_case` code such as `invalid_credentials`. The set may grow in a minor release.                                                                                                                                |
| `identifierHmac`  | string                                        | no       | A keyed HMAC (HMAC-SHA-256, base64url) of the identifier the person typed, so repeated attempts at one identifier can be correlated without revealing it. Absent when the attempt named a known user, who is then the subject. |
| `verifierProfile` | string                                        | no       | The verifier profile the wallet presentation was checked under, such as `haip-1.0`.                                                                                                                                            |

### authorization.failed v1

The authorization endpoint refused a request: an unknown client, a redirect URI that is not registered, a scope the client may not have, or a denial.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:authorization.failed:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `warning` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`
- Schema: [authorization.failed.v1.json](/schemas/events/authorization.failed.v1.json)

| Member   | Type   | Required | Meaning                                                                                         |
| -------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `error`  | string | yes      | The OAuth or OpenID Connect `error` code the request was refused with, such as `invalid_grant`. |
| `reason` | string | no       | Why, as a `snake_case` code such as `invalid_credentials`. The set may grow in a minor release. |

### step_up.required v1

A request needs a fresh sign-in or new consent before it can go on, for example for a dangerous scope (ADR-007 §2).

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:step_up.required:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`
- Schema: [step_up.required.v1.json](/schemas/events/step_up.required.v1.json)

| Member            | Type            | Required | Meaning                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | --------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `reason`          | string          | yes      | Why, as a `snake_case` code such as `invalid_credentials`. The set may grow in a minor release. |
| `error`           | string          | no       | The OAuth or OpenID Connect `error` code the request was refused with, such as `invalid_grant`. |
| `elevatedScopes`  | array of string | no       | The scopes the request adds to what the user already granted.                                   |
| `dangerousScopes` | array of string | no       | The requested scopes classed as dangerous.                                                      |
| `prompt`          | string          | no       | The OpenID Connect `prompt` value of the request.                                               |
| `maxAge`          | integer         | no       | The `max_age` of the request, in seconds.                                                       |

After a fresh sign-in, a user granted a client dangerous scopes (ADR-007 §2).

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:step_up.elevated:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`

### token.issued v1

The token endpoint issued tokens: for an authorization code, a refresh, client credentials, a token exchange or a JWT bearer assertion.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:token.issued:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`
- Schema: [token.issued.v1.json](/schemas/events/token.issued.v1.json)

| Member            | Type                                                 | Required | Meaning                                                                                                       |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `grantType`       | string                                               | yes      | The `grant_type` of the token request, such as `authorization_code`.                                          |
| `scopes`          | array of string                                      | no       | The scopes of the issued access token.                                                                        |
| `audience`        | array of string                                      | no       | The audience of the issued token.                                                                             |
| `resources`       | array of string                                      | no       | The RFC 8707 resource indicators the token is bound to.                                                       |
| `expiresIn`       | integer                                              | no       | The lifetime of the issued access token, in seconds.                                                          |
| `issuedTokenType` | string                                               | no       | The RFC 8693 `issued_token_type` of a token exchange.                                                         |
| `refreshFamilyId` | UUID                                                 | no       | The refresh family the issued refresh token belongs to. Every rotation keeps it.                              |
| `delegationDepth` | integer                                              | no       | How many actors the RFC 8693 `act` chain of the issued token holds.                                           |
| `idJagId`         | string                                               | no       | The `jti` of the identity assertion authorization grant minted or consumed (ADR-011). Never the grant itself. |
| `idJagIssuer`     | string                                               | no       | The issuer of a consumed identity assertion authorization grant (ADR-011).                                    |
| `scopeMode`       | one of `readonly`, `admin`, `exec`, or a later value | no       | The agent scope mode (ADR-007 §2) the request was granted: `readonly`, `admin` or `exec`.                     |

| Member      | Type   | Required | Meaning                                                                                         |
| ----------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `grantType` | string | no       | The `grant_type` of the token request, such as `authorization_code`.                            |
| `error`     | string | yes      | The OAuth or OpenID Connect `error` code the request was refused with, such as `invalid_grant`. |
| `reason`    | string | no       | Why, as a `snake_case` code such as `invalid_credentials`. The set may grow in a minor release. |

### token.revoked v1

A client revoked a token at the RFC 7009 revocation endpoint.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:token.revoked:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`
- Schema: [token.revoked.v1.json](/schemas/events/token.revoked.v1.json)

| Member     | Type   | Required | Meaning                                                         |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `typeHint` | string | no       | The `token_type_hint` the client sent, such as `refresh_token`. |

### token.revocation_failed v1

The revocation endpoint refused a request, for example on failed client authentication.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:token.revocation_failed:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `warning` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: none
- Schema: [token.revocation_failed.v1.json](/schemas/events/token.revocation_failed.v1.json)

| Member   | Type   | Required | Meaning                                                                                         |
| -------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `error`  | string | yes      | The OAuth or OpenID Connect `error` code the request was refused with, such as `invalid_grant`. |
| `reason` | string | no       | Why, as a `snake_case` code such as `invalid_credentials`. The set may grow in a minor release. |

### token.introspected v1

A resource server introspected an active token (RFC 7662).

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:token.introspected:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`
- Schema: [token.introspected.v1.json](/schemas/events/token.introspected.v1.json)

| Member          | Type   | Required | Meaning                                               |
| --------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `tokenClientId` | string | no       | The `client_id` the introspected token was issued to. |

### token.introspection_failed v1

An introspection request failed: client authentication, or a token that is invalid, expired, revoked or not one the caller may inspect.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:token.introspection_failed:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `warning` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: none
- Schema: [token.introspection_failed.v1.json](/schemas/events/token.introspection_failed.v1.json)

| Member   | Type   | Required | Meaning                                                                                         |
| -------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `error`  | string | yes      | The OAuth or OpenID Connect `error` code the request was refused with, such as `invalid_grant`. |
| `reason` | string | no       | Why, as a `snake_case` code such as `invalid_credentials`. The set may grow in a minor release. |

### userinfo.served v1

The userinfo endpoint returned claims for an access token.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:userinfo.served:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`
- Schema: [userinfo.served.v1.json](/schemas/events/userinfo.served.v1.json)

`data` has no members: the envelope carries the event.

### userinfo.request_failed v1

The userinfo endpoint refused a request.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:userinfo.request_failed:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `warning` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: none
- Schema: [userinfo.request_failed.v1.json](/schemas/events/userinfo.request_failed.v1.json)

| Member   | Type   | Required | Meaning                                                                                         |
| -------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `error`  | string | yes      | The OAuth or OpenID Connect `error` code the request was refused with, such as `invalid_grant`. |
| `reason` | string | no       | Why, as a `snake_case` code such as `invalid_credentials`. The set may grow in a minor release. |

### client.created v1

An OAuth client was created: by RFC 7591 dynamic registration, or by a developer through the developer API.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:client.created:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `client`
- Schema: [client.created.v1.json](/schemas/events/client.created.v1.json)

| Member         | Type                                                | Required | Meaning                                                                                                                        |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `registration` | one of `dynamic`, `developer_api`, or a later value | yes      | `dynamic`: RFC 7591 dynamic client registration. `developer_api`: a developer created it. The set may grow in a minor release. |
| `isPublic`     | boolean                                             | yes      | Whether the client is public, with no client authentication.                                                                   |
| `isAgent`      | boolean                                             | no       | Whether the client registered as an agent (ADR-007 §2).                                                                        |
| `grantTypes`   | array of string                                     | yes      | The grant types the client may use.                                                                                            |
| `scopes`       | array of string                                     | no       | The scopes the client may request.                                                                                             |
| `authMethod`   | string                                              | no       | How the client authenticates at the token endpoint, such as `private_key_jwt`.                                                 |

### client.updated v1

A developer changed a client's settings.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:client.updated:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `client`
- Schema: [client.updated.v1.json](/schemas/events/client.updated.v1.json)

| Member   | Type            | Required | Meaning                                                     |
| -------- | --------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `fields` | array of string | yes      | The names of the settings that changed. Never their values. |

### client.deleted v1

A developer deleted a client.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:client.deleted:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `client`
- Schema: [client.deleted.v1.json](/schemas/events/client.deleted.v1.json)

`data` has no members: the envelope carries the event.

### client.secret_rotated v1

A developer replaced a client's secret. The old secret stopped working.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:client.secret_rotated:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `client`
- Schema: [client.secret_rotated.v1.json](/schemas/events/client.secret_rotated.v1.json)

`data` has no members: the envelope carries the event.

### client.suspended v1

An operator suspended a client: it can no longer obtain tokens until the suspension is lifted.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:client.suspended:v1`
- Category: `admin` · Severity: `warning` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `client`
- Schema: [client.suspended.v1.json](/schemas/events/client.suspended.v1.json)

`data` has no members: the envelope carries the event.

### client.suspension_lifted v1

An operator lifted a client's suspension.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:client.suspension_lifted:v1`
- Category: `admin` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `client`
- Schema: [client.suspension_lifted.v1.json](/schemas/events/client.suspension_lifted.v1.json)

`data` has no members: the envelope carries the event.

### api_key.created v1

A developer created an API key for a client.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:api_key.created:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `api_key`
- Schema: [api_key.created.v1.json](/schemas/events/api_key.created.v1.json)

`data` has no members: the envelope carries the event.

### api_key.revoked v1

A developer revoked an API key. It stopped working.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:api_key.revoked:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `api_key`
- Schema: [api_key.revoked.v1.json](/schemas/events/api_key.revoked.v1.json)

`data` has no members: the envelope carries the event.

### wallet.linked v1

A signed-in user linked a wallet credential to their account.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:wallet.linked:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`
- Schema: [wallet.linked.v1.json](/schemas/events/wallet.linked.v1.json)

| Member            | Type    | Required | Meaning                                                                             |
| ----------------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `credentialId`    | string  | yes      | The id of the account credential the wallet was linked as.                          |
| `subjectSource`   | string  | yes      | How the subject was resolved from the presentation (ADR-009).                       |
| `rebound`         | boolean | yes      | Whether the link replaced an earlier binding of the same credential.                |
| `verifierProfile` | string  | yes      | The verifier profile the wallet presentation was checked under, such as `haip-1.0`. |

### wallet.link_failed v1

A wallet could not be linked, for example because it is linked to another account.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:wallet.link_failed:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `warning` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`
- Schema: [wallet.link_failed.v1.json](/schemas/events/wallet.link_failed.v1.json)

| Member            | Type   | Required | Meaning                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `reason`          | string | yes      | Why, as a `snake_case` code such as `invalid_credentials`. The set may grow in a minor release. |
| `verifierProfile` | string | no       | The verifier profile the wallet presentation was checked under, such as `haip-1.0`.             |

### wallet.presentation_received v1

The OpenID4VP response endpoint accepted a wallet presentation. This is not a sign-in: the flow that asked for it decides.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:wallet.presentation_received:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `info` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: none
- Schema: [wallet.presentation_received.v1.json](/schemas/events/wallet.presentation_received.v1.json)

| Member              | Type    | Required | Meaning                                                                             |
| ------------------- | ------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `verifierProfile`   | string  | yes      | The verifier profile the wallet presentation was checked under, such as `haip-1.0`. |
| `presentationCount` | integer | yes      | How many presentations the response held.                                           |

### request.csrf_rejected v1

A form post was refused because its CSRF check failed: the token was missing or did not match.

- Identifier: `urn:qauth:event:request.csrf_rejected:v1`
- Category: `user` · Severity: `warning` · Since: v0.2.0
- Subject: `user`
- Schema: [request.csrf_rejected.v1.json](/schemas/events/request.csrf_rejected.v1.json)

| Member | Type                                                                                                 | Required | Meaning                                                        |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `form` | one of `sign_in`, `wallet_sign_in`, `wallet_link`, `consent`, `consent_revocation`, or a later value | yes      | The form that was posted. The set may grow in a minor release. |

## Earlier event names

Before the event contract, QAuth wrote free-form event names to its audit log and its log
lines. Each becomes a registered type. Several earlier names become one type, and the name implied
some `data`, which an audit row copied into the event store receives.

| Earlier name                      | Written to | Type                                              | Implied `data`                |
| --------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `user.login.success`              | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:user.signed_in:v1`               | `method: password`            |
| `user.login.failure`              | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:user.sign_in_failed:v1`          | `method: password`            |
| `ui.login.success`                | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:user.signed_in:v1`               | `method: password`            |
| `ui.login.failure`                | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:user.sign_in_failed:v1`          | `method: password`            |
| `ui.login.csrf_failure`           | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:request.csrf_rejected:v1`        | `form: sign_in`               |
| `ui.wallet_login.success`         | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:user.signed_in:v1`               | `method: wallet`              |
| `ui.wallet_login.failure`         | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:user.sign_in_failed:v1`          | `method: wallet`              |
| `ui.wallet_login.csrf_failure`    | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:request.csrf_rejected:v1`        | `form: wallet_sign_in`        |
| `user.logout.success`             | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:user.signed_out:v1`              | —                             |
| `user.logout.failure`             | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:user.sign_out_failed:v1`         | —                             |
| `user.register.success`           | log line   | `urn:qauth:event:user.registered:v1`              | `method: password`            |
| `user.register.failure`           | log line   | `urn:qauth:event:user.registration_failed:v1`     | —                             |
| `oauth.authorize.success`         | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:authorization.completed:v1`      | —                             |
| `oauth.authorize.failure`         | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:authorization.failed:v1`         | —                             |
| `oauth.stepup.required`           | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:step_up.required:v1`             | —                             |
| `oauth.stepup.elevation`          | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:step_up.elevated:v1`             | —                             |
| `oauth.consent.granted`           | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:consent.granted:v1`              | —                             |
| `oauth.consent.denied`            | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:consent.denied:v1`               | —                             |
| `oauth.consent.revoked`           | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:consent.revoked:v1`              | —                             |
| `oauth.consent.csrf_failure`      | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:request.csrf_rejected:v1`        | `form: consent`               |
| `consents.revoke.csrf_failure`    | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:request.csrf_rejected:v1`        | `form: consent_revocation`    |
| `oauth.token.exchange.success`    | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:token.issued:v1`                 | —                             |
| `oauth.token.exchange.failure`    | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:token.request_failed:v1`         | —                             |
| `oauth.revoke.success`            | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:token.revoked:v1`                | —                             |
| `oauth.revoke.failure`            | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:token.revocation_failed:v1`      | —                             |
| `oauth.introspect.success`        | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:token.introspected:v1`           | —                             |
| `oauth.introspect.failure`        | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:token.introspection_failed:v1`   | —                             |
| `oauth.userinfo.success`          | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:userinfo.served:v1`              | —                             |
| `oauth.userinfo.failure`          | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:userinfo.request_failed:v1`      | —                             |
| `oauth.client.registered`         | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:client.created:v1`               | `registration: dynamic`       |
| `oauth.client.created`            | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:client.created:v1`               | `registration: developer_api` |
| `oauth.client.updated`            | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:client.updated:v1`               | —                             |
| `oauth.client.deleted`            | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:client.deleted:v1`               | —                             |
| `oauth.client.secret_regenerated` | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:client.secret_rotated:v1`        | —                             |
| `oauth.client.suspended`          | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:client.suspended:v1`             | —                             |
| `oauth.client.suspension_lifted`  | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:client.suspension_lifted:v1`     | —                             |
| `api_key.created`                 | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:api_key.created:v1`              | —                             |
| `api_key.revoked`                 | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:api_key.revoked:v1`              | —                             |
| `auth.wallet_link.success`        | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:wallet.linked:v1`                | —                             |
| `auth.wallet_link.failure`        | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:wallet.link_failed:v1`           | —                             |
| `auth.wallet_link.csrf_failure`   | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:request.csrf_rejected:v1`        | `form: wallet_link`           |
| `oid4vp.response.received`        | audit log  | `urn:qauth:event:wallet.presentation_received:v1` | —                             |
